text:
Srimad Bhagavad Gita

[Chapter 9, Verses 30-31]

Shridhara Swami’s Commentary: If You grant liberation only to Your devotees, and not to non-devotees, does this mean You possess partiality born of attachment or aversion? Addressing this, He says, "I am the same." I am equal toward all beings; therefore, there is no one who is dear to Me or detestable to Me. Although this is true, those who worship Me, they are in Me as devotees, and I am in them as the Bestower of Grace. The essence is this: just as fire does not act with partiality when it removes the suffering of cold and darkness only for those who approach it, or just as the wish-fulfilling tree <note>The <term>kalpavriksha</term> <gloss>wish-fulfilling tree of Hindu mythology</gloss></note> acts without bias, similarly, there is no partiality in Me, even though I favor My devotees. Rather, this is the inherent greatness of devotion to Me. (29)

Madhusudana Saraswati’s Commentary: Furthermore, the greatness of devotion to Me is such that it creates this appearance of partiality even in One who is equal. Hear of that greatness:

> Even if a person of very wicked conduct worships Me with single-minded devotion, he is to be regarded as righteous, for he has resolved correctly. (30)

Whoever he may be, even if he is a person of very wicked conduct, like Ajamila, if he worships Me with single-minded devotion—serving Me due to the dawning of some past merit—he, though previously unrighteous, must be regarded as righteous. For he has resolved correctly; that is, he has attained a righteous determination. (30)

Shridhara Swami’s Commentary: Furthermore, showing that the power of devotion to Me is beyond logic, He says, "Even if." Even a man of extremely wicked conduct, if he worships only Me—Shri Narayana—without practicing devotion to other deities, he is to be regarded as righteous, as excellent. Because he has resolved correctly; he has made the firm determination that "I shall be fulfilled by worshipping the Supreme Lord alone." (30)

Madhusudana Saraswati’s Commentary: Because of this very correct determination, he abandons his wicked conduct:

> Quickly he becomes a soul of righteousness and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, proclaim that My devotee never perishes. (31)

Even one who was unrighteous for a long time quickly becomes a soul of righteousness—one whose mind follows righteousness—due to the greatness of worshipping Me. He abandons his wicked conduct instantly and becomes well-behaved. Moreover, he attains lasting peace; he thoroughly attains permanent cessation of the desire for sense objects, due to extreme detachment. One might think: "Perhaps a devotee of Mine, not having abandoned his previously practiced wicked conduct, might not become righteous, and thus he would surely perish." Denying this, out of compassion for His devotees, the Lord speaks as if provoked: Do not consider this a wonder, O son of Kunti. The greatness of devotion to Me is certainly such as this. Therefore, even in front of those who are skeptical, make a promise. Make this pledge with boldness and confidence: "My devotee—the devotee of Vasudeva—even if he is of very wicked conduct, even if he faces a crisis of life, even if he is entreated by those worthy of things hard to attain, even if he is extremely ignorant or without shelter, does not perish. Rather, he is fulfilled."

<summary>This page contains commentary on Bhagavad Gita 9.30-31, explaining that the Lord's perceived partiality toward devotees is actually the inherent power of devotion itself, which transforms even the most wicked individuals into righteous souls.</summary>
